zones.name: Hearthwood
zones.gate: Three ordinary proofs, shown to the guard on the north road
zones.blurb: A wooded river valley where every mage begins.
zones.arrival: Alders lean over the water, and the whole valley smells of wet bark and woodsmoke. Someone is sharpening something. Nobody looks up when you pass, which is its own kind of welcome.

zones.name: Whispering Woods
zones.blurb: Sun-dappled woods that murmur when nothing is moving them.
zones.arrival: Sun comes down through the leaves in pieces and moves when they move. It is a good path, well walked, and the air smells of warm bark. Somewhere under it all, something is murmuring.
beats: The murmur stops the moment you stand still to listen. When you walk on, it starts again.
You have passed this bend before. The path has not looped — you have been watching for that. The trees have moved.
It is not coming from the trees. It is coming from underneath them, from the roots crossing beneath the path, and it is all one sound. You have been walking on it this whole time.
zones.epilogue: The murmur does not stop when the heartwood comes down. It moves — under the path, out toward the edges, somewhere you cannot walk to — and settles there. You did not kill anything. You interrupted something, and it noticed you doing it.

zones.name: Glimmerbrook
zones.blurb: Springs and shallows east of Hearthwood, bright enough to hurt.
zones.arrival: The brook runs over pale stones and throws the light back at you in pieces. Fish hang in the current without swimming. The water is colder than the season should allow.

zones.name: Cinderpeak Foothills
zones.blurb: The first rise north, where the ground is warm through your boots.
zones.arrival: The grass gives out and the slope turns to grey grit that shifts under you. Somewhere above, the mountain is breathing. The air tastes of struck flint.

zones.name: Thornmire
zones.blurb: Where the woods drown in the brook's outflow.
zones.arrival: The path becomes a suggestion, then a rumour, then water. Trees stand in it up to their knees and have made peace with that. Everything green here is winning.

zones.name: Ashfall Vale
zones.blurb: Downwind of the cone: the burn scar where ash falls on forest.
zones.arrival: Grey settles on every leaf until the whole valley looks like a charcoal drawing of itself. New shoots are already pushing up through it. Fire came through here, and something is arguing about whether it won.

zones.name: Pennycross
zones.blurb: The first market, where the river road crosses the mountain road.
zones.arrival: Two roads meet and a town happened. Stalls have grown into buildings, and the buildings still look like stalls. Everyone is halfway through a transaction.

zones.name: Forgeholm
zones.blurb: A city with a mountain for a roof, cut into the Ironspine.
zones.arrival: You arrive at a door. The road ends at a gate in the rock and everything past it was cut rather than built — halls stacked over halls, stairs where a street would be, and a red glow a long way down that never goes out. Ore does not leave here until it has a name. It is never quiet and never cold.

zones.name: Old Quarry
zones.blurb: Cut into the range's southern flank, and cut too deep.
zones.arrival: The road stops being a road and becomes the floor of something somebody dug. Terraces step down into shadow, each one squarer than anything nature makes, and the tool marks are old. Whatever was quarried out of here left a shape, and the shape has started to move.

zones.name: Stormcliff Coast
zones.blurb: Where the western ocean's weather hits a wall and has nowhere to go.
zones.arrival: The cliffs take the whole weight of it. Spray comes up further than it should and your hair lifts before you hear the crack. The rock is scorched in long vertical lines.

zones.name: Galehaven
zones.blurb: The one notch in a hundred miles of cliff.
zones.arrival: The harbour is impossibly calm for what is happening outside it. Cloth and dye come off the boats in bales; nothing here is made locally except the ships.

zones.name: Windward Steppe
zones.blurb: A high tableland east of the crest, scoured flat.
zones.arrival: Nothing here is taller than your knee, and everything leans the same way. The wind does not gust; it simply blows, and has been blowing since before there was anyone to notice.

zones.name: Frostfell Pass
zones.blurb: The way through. Sea air lifted over the crest and frozen there.
zones.arrival: The pass is a white corridor between two black walls. Your breath goes up and does not come down. The road is under here somewhere, and other people have been sure of that too.

zones.name: Thunderspire Peaks
zones.blurb: The summit line where coastal storm meets steppe wind.
zones.arrival: You are inside the weather rather than under it. The cloud is lit from within at intervals, and the intervals are getting shorter. Metal hums.

zones.name: The Molten Deep
zones.blurb: Under the quarry, under the mountain, under the sea's level.
zones.arrival: The quarry's deepest gallery keeps going after the tool marks stop. The rock gets warm, then hot, then lit from below. There is a floor down here that moves like water because it is not water.

zones.name: Concordance
zones.gate: The Kinetic Sigil, in three parts, shown at the gate
zones.blurb: The trade capital, at the head of navigation on the River Concord.
zones.arrival: Everything that moves by water or road in this world passes through here, and the city has arranged itself around that fact. You show your Sigil at the gate. Nobody fights you; someone writes your name down.

zones.name: The Kiln Desert
zones.blurb: A cold high desert in the range's rain shadow, and the sunniest ground in the world.
zones.arrival: The air is too thin to hold heat, so the sun burns while the wind bites. There is no shade anywhere and no water for a day's walk. Your shadow is the hardest-edged thing you have ever seen.

zones.name: The Mirrormere
zones.blurb: A high still lake that holds the moon better than the sky does.
zones.arrival: Not a ripple. The surface gives you back the mountains, the stars, and the moon at a size the moon has no right to be. Walking the shore, you are careful not to look down for too long.

zones.name: Starfall Basin
zones.blurb: A crater field, preserved because nothing grows to cover it.
zones.arrival: Bowl after bowl in the pale ground, each with something at the bottom that is not from here. Nothing has grown over them because nothing grows. At night the sky is so clear it looks like a threat.

zones.name: Meridian
zones.blurb: An observatory on the crest of the Scarp: the highest dark-sky ground there is.
zones.arrival: A town of long roofs that open. Everyone keeps different hours and nobody explains. From the crest you can see the desert on one side and, on the other, a valley with no light in it at all.

zones.name: Tidewrack Shoals
zones.blurb: Tides that obey the moon exactly, on the northern shore.
zones.arrival: The water goes out further than seems survivable and comes back faster. What it uncovers has been down there a long time. Everything is timed to something overhead.

zones.name: The Sunless Reach
zones.blurb: The Scarp's north face. Direct sun never reaches the floor.
zones.arrival: You come over the crest out of glare into a valley that has never been lit. The rock is the same rock. The desert is a thousand feet away and on the other side of the world.

zones.name: The Shattered Orrery
zones.blurb: A broken model of the heavens, still trying to run.
zones.arrival: Rings the size of bridges, half of them fallen, and the fallen half still turning. The arcing is not weather; it is the mechanism. Something is being calculated and has been for a very long time.

zones.name: Rimeholt
zones.gate: A Celestial Totem charged with the Solar, Lunar and Astral essences, to pass the barrier above the town
zones.blurb: Basecamp. The last mortal outpost, above the tree line.
zones.arrival: There is no wood here, so nothing is built of it. The town is stone and rope and hide, dug in against a slope that goes up out of sight. Everyone you meet is either arriving or leaving; nobody is from here.

zones.name: Hallowmarch
zones.blurb: The Vault's south flank: a consecrated causeway up the only side that thaws.
zones.arrival: A raised road, and someone built it. The sun reaches this face for a few hours and the meltwater runs beside you the whole way. Every mile or so there is a marker, and every marker has been maintained.

zones.name: The Umbral Wastes
zones.blurb: The Vault's north face. No direct sun at any hour of any day.
zones.arrival: You round the shoulder and the light stops. Not dusk — an absence with an edge to it. The ice here has never melted and holds its shape like something that has been thought about.

zones.name: The Reliquary Deep
zones.blurb: A vault bored through the mountain from the lit side to the dark.
zones.arrival: The door is on the warm flank and the far end opens onto the ice. In between, a corridor that someone consecrated and someone else did not leave alone. It is warmer in the middle than at either end.

zones.name: Vespergate
zones.blurb: Where the ground runs out. The last place with a supply line.
zones.arrival: A fortress at the top of the world, facing the wrong way — not outward at an enemy but upward, at nothing. Above it the rock goes vertical and stops being a route. They have been brewing their own everything for a long time.

zones.name: The Sealed Garden
zones.blurb: A garden nobody has been let into for a very long time.
zones.arrival: The wall is low enough to see over and that is the whole cruelty of it. Inside, everything is in leaf and in season at once. The gate is shut, the guard is still at the gate, and the faith that posted him has been gone for centuries.

zones.name: The Glass Archive
zones.blurb: They wrote it in light, and light does not keep.
zones.arrival: Lenses on every roof, and all of them still aimed. Around midday the hillside fills with writing you can almost read, and by the time your eyes adjust it has moved on. Whatever they recorded here, they recorded onto the one thing that will not hold still.

zones.name: The Buried Sky
zones.blurb: The oldest rock in the world, and it is full of stars.
zones.arrival: You climb to the top of everything in order to go down. The shaft cuts through band after band of stone, and every band holds a scatter of light in it. None of the patterns match the sky you walked in under.

zones.name: The Collapsed Academy
zones.blurb: A school that read too far, and left.
zones.arrival: It is not ruined so much as unfinished in the wrong direction. Staircases arrive at rooms that were never built. The syllabus is still on the wall and the last three items on it are not in any language you have.

zones.name: The Unwritten Library
zones.blurb: Knowledge that eats its keeper. The shelves are still filling.
zones.arrival: Every book here is being written right now, by nobody. The shelves go up past where a ceiling would be. Something is taking dictation and it would like your name for the record.

zones.name: The Eclipsed Citadel
zones.blurb: The door back into the world, and the thing standing in it.
zones.arrival: Below it, through a gap in nothing, is the summit of the mountain you could not climb. The Citadel is between you and it. That is what the name has always meant.

zones.name: Zenith
zones.station: Every station — the only town with all six
zones.gate: The Concordant Crown: twelve elemental gems and twelve Cores, bound with a purchased binding spell
zones.blurb: The summit. Visible from everywhere below, and shut.
zones.arrival: The doors were never locked from the inside. From up here the whole world is one thing, and every city you have ever walked into is a mark on it you could put a finger over.

creatures.name: Listening Fawn
creatures.lore: It does not flee and it does not approach. Twice I have looked up to find it closer without having seen it move, and both times it was facing the ground rather than me.

creatures.name: Thornback Sprite
creatures.lore: Small, and gone before the swing finishes. The thorns are not for defence — it plants them, and comes back for them later.

creatures.name: Sporecap Shambler
creatures.lore: The cap is the animal and the body is scaffolding. Cut the body and the cap simply builds another, more slowly and slightly wrong.

creatures.name: Bindweed Creeper
creatures.lore: It drinks. Everything in this wood that stands still long enough is eventually part of the same drink, and it is patient about it.

creatures.name: Rootknuckle
creatures.lore: A knot of root that comes up through the path where the path is thinnest. It is not hunting. You are simply standing on it.

creatures.name: Elderroot
creatures.lore: Older than the path, and the path was surveyed twice. It has been doing this longer than anything else here and it shows.

creatures.name: Mother Spore
creatures.lore: Every shambler in the wood is hers, and she does not appear to care about any of them individually.

creatures.name: Hollow Stag
creatures.lore: What is left of a Listening Fawn that listened for long enough. It is still facing the ground.

creatures.name: The Murmur
creatures.lore: The sound the whole wood makes, standing in one place for once. It knows the shape of what you were about to do.

creatures.name: Heartwood
creatures.lore: Everything under the path runs back to here. Standing at its base, the murmur is not a sound any more; it is a pressure.

creatures.name: The Standing Green
creatures.lore: The wood grew this in the shape of a person, and got the proportions nearly right. It is the "nearly" that stays with you.

creatures.name: Brook Naiad
creatures.lore: A child-sized figure of clear water with pale stones hanging inside it where organs should be. Its edge is sharp, not misty, which is the detail that stops it looking like weather.

creatures.name: Shiverfish Shoal
creatures.lore: Forty fish holding one shape, too rigidly to be natural. It casts a single shadow, and I have not yet seen a fish leave it.

creatures.name: Glassfleck Wisp
creatures.lore: Made of the light off the water rather than of the water. It throws the brightness back at you in pieces, and looks as though touching it would end the argument.

creatures.name: Siltback Crawler
creatures.lore: A crayfish crossed with a boulder, low to the riverbed and crusted over with weed. Two eyes on stalks, set close, and both of them on you the whole time.

creatures.name: Chill Eel
creatures.lore: Bone-white and nearly clear, held straight rather than coiled. Frost forms on the water around it while it is doing nothing whatsoever.

creatures.name: Weirkeeper
creatures.lore: A man built out of the beams of an old weir, wet timber and river stone, water pouring steadily through the gaps in its chest. It carries nothing, because it does not need to.

creatures.name: The Held Breath
creatures.lore: One bubble of air taller than a man, held under and refusing to rise. There is a curled shape inside it. I have written down twice that it is a thing being kept, not a thing swimming.

creatures.name: Pale Coil
creatures.lore: An eel as thick as a man's waist and three times his length, coiled once with the head up. Blind. The water around it is noticeably clearer than the rest, which I would rather not think about.

creatures.name: Frostgleam Naiad
creatures.lore: A Brook Naiad grown up and half frozen — ice blooming across her shoulders and brow while the rest of her still runs. She is not in any hurry, and the stones inside her have stopped moving.

creatures.name: The Cold Below
creatures.lore: Broad, flat and wider than a house, seen through water that should not be deep enough to hold it. Only part of it is ever visible. The rest goes down into black and keeps going.

creatures.name: Stillwater
creatures.lore: Three storeys of standing pool, mirror-flat on every face, with no features of any kind. It reflects whoever is in front of it. Nothing inside it moves, and that is the entire horror of the thing.

creatures.name: Ashjaw Brute
creatures.lore: Ox-sized, and caked in grey ash that has dried and cracked like a riverbed. There is orange light in the cracks. It stands square and keeps its head low, which is not deference.

creatures.name: Flint Skink
creatures.lore: Forearm-length, and its scales are knapped flint — faceted, dark, and glowing orange between the plates. It crosses rock too hot to stand on and does not appear to notice.

creatures.name: Cinder Moth
creatures.lore: Two hands across, wings a translucent ash-grey shot through with ember veins that brighten toward the body. It looks one touch from disintegrating, and that turns out to be accurate.

creatures.name: Slagshell Tortoise
creatures.lore: The shell is one lump of cooled lava, pitted and cracked with dull red still down in the fissures. The face underneath it is ancient and entirely patient. It draws in slightly and waits you out.

creatures.name: Ventworm
creatures.lore: Half out of a fissure and as long as a man, dull red-brown and segmented. Its front end is a ring of small plates rather than a mouth, and sulphur comes out of it steadily whether or not it moves.

creatures.name: Slagheart
creatures.lore: A man-shape of cooled black lava, cracked throughout, with one fist-sized cavity in the chest and a molten core sitting in it. The arms do not match. It moves deliberately and it is balanced.

creatures.name: Vent Warden
creatures.lore: Twice as wide as a man and barely taller, fused slag and black basalt, with its legs sunk into the rock over a fissure. Its whole chest is a grate glowing deep orange. There is no head; the shoulders simply end.

creatures.name: Char-Tusk
creatures.lore: A boar shoulder-high to a man, hide burnt black and split with glowing seams, two great upward tusks of cracked stone with the tips still hot. It puts one foreleg forward and then does not move again.

creatures.name: The Emberqueen
creatures.lore: A moth the size of a large dog, wings a deep smouldering red held wide and scorched into a pattern I could not copy accurately. She displays rather than beats them. She has not once tried to leave.

creatures.name: The Breathing Stone
creatures.lore: Four storeys of grey rock and scree in the rough shape of something hunched. The fissures down its back widen and narrow, slowly, in time. Vapour comes off its shoulders. It is the mountain, and the mountain is what has been breathing.

creatures.name: Flintmaw
creatures.lore: A great cat rendered in fractured volcanic glass, horse-sized and low, every plane sharp and faintly reflective with molten orange in the seams between. The jaw is too long. It watches, and it waits, and it is clearly deciding something.

creatures.name: Mirewalker
creatures.lore: Tall, thin and long in the limb, black waterlogged wood hung with weed, wading upright. Bog water runs out of its joints the whole time. Its head is a narrow bud with nothing on it.

creatures.name: Thirstvine
creatures.lore: Coiled like a python and swollen tight with what it has taken. Where it has fed the vine is fat and bright; where it has not, it is thin and grey. You can read its week off it.

creatures.name: Leechcap
creatures.lore: A plate-sized mushroom of wet dark red travelling gill-side down on a fringe of pale feelers. The underside spirals in to a small dark opening. Water runs off the cap and never into it.

creatures.name: Bog Lantern
creatures.lore: A seed-head the size of a man's head floating at chest height, lit greenish-white from inside, trailing a crown of fine filaments. The light is warm. The thing itself is not.

creatures.name: Reedback Lurker
creatures.lore: Boat-sized, half submerged, its back a plate of green-black shell so overgrown with living reed that it reads as a piece of the bank. Two small dark eyes at the waterline. I walked past it twice.

creatures.name: Old Wallow
creatures.lore: Cart-sized, low and broad like a hippopotamus, and so thoroughly overgrown with moss and ferns and small saplings that the animal is a rumour under a garden. Small eyes, set high. Half out of the water.

creatures.name: The Green Drowning
creatures.lore: A standing wall of matted weed and root three times a man's height and as wide, rising sheer out of the bog with water pouring off it without stopping. No limbs. No face. It advances.

creatures.name: Wickerdrowned
creatures.lore: A man-shape woven out of wet withies, hollow all the way through, with black water sloshing audibly inside the ribs. The arms have been sharpened. The head is a woven cage, tilted, listening.

creatures.name: Fenmother
creatures.lore: Hunched and broad-hipped, twice a man's bulk, woven reed over black mud and standing waist-deep. Her arms are long bundles of dripping root. Where a face should be there is a mat of green weed, hanging.

creatures.name: Mirethroat
creatures.lore: A ring of dark muscular plant matter wider than a house, lying level with the bog and opening into a funnel lined with rows of soft inward-pointing spines. The water spirals into it, slowly, always.

creatures.name: The Drinking Grove
creatures.lore: Six drowned trees that have grown into one four-storey creature, trunks fused and canopy shared. Its roots are lifted clear of the water and end in a thicket of pale swollen tendrils, all dripping. The high branches are in full leaf and perfectly healthy.

creatures.name: Cinderbloom Husk
creatures.lore: A burnt stalk the height of a man, hollow and brittle, topped with a charred seed head that sheds grey without stopping. Green shoots have already broken through the black stem. It walks on stiff roots.

creatures.name: Ashroot Sapling
creatures.lore: No taller than a man, bark scorched black down one side and pale green down the other, walking on a splay of roots. The roots are visibly drawing ash up into the trunk, and the green side is the better for it.

creatures.name: Emberseed
creatures.lore: A melon-sized pod hovering a hand above the ground, husk cracked open in a spiral around a fiercely glowing core. Charred filaments trail behind it. Everything about it reads as about to burst.

creatures.name: Scorchmoth
creatures.lore: Hand-sized and narrow in the wing, sooty black with tiny bright green spots across it like new leaves. Thin body, long legs, and it does not hold still long enough to be counted. Ash falls around it constantly.

creatures.name: Charwood Walker
creatures.lore: A dead tree twice a man's height, charred and stripped, walking on two thick root-legs with branches for arms. Dull orange heat still sits in the cracks. One green branch grows from a shoulder, and it has not been shed.

creatures.name: The Grey Stag
creatures.lore: A tall stag the colour of cold ash, coat gone uniform grey, antlers burnt black at the tips. Small green leaves are growing from the base of the antlers. It raises its head and it does not run.

creatures.name: First Green
creatures.lore: A thicket of new growth risen into a squat figure twice a man's width, every surface crowded with bright young leaves. Underneath the green there are glimpses of blackened wood. It is rooted, and it does not intend to move.

creatures.name: Last Ember
creatures.lore: Man-height and thin as a whip, charcoal and living flame, trailing sparks it does not seem to miss. Cracked black over white heat all the way down. There is nothing green on it anywhere.

creatures.name: Kindleroot
creatures.lore: A cart-wide sprawl of root lifted up off the ground, every tip glowing orange like a slow match. Wherever it has crossed there are small fires and small shoots, both, in the same tracks. It has no head at all.

creatures.name: The Blackened Crown
creatures.lore: Four storeys of burnt heartwood in roughly the shape of a man, broad in the shoulder, upright, still. The head is ringed with charred branches burning steadily and white. Nothing grows on it. It looks like it won.

creatures.name: The Rooting
creatures.lore: A mound of new growth four storeys across and only two high, made of thousands of young saplings and ferns and vines grown together. Burnt timber and old bones are visible inside it, being swallowed. It looks like it is winning.

items.name: Oak Log
items.lore: Cut green, it weeps for a week. Hearthwood seasons it in the open because the smoke gets into anything dried indoors.

items.name: Bindweed Fibre
items.lore: Strong out of all proportion to its thickness. The trick is cutting it before it notices.

items.name: Flora Dust
items.lore: What a growing thing leaves when it is unmade faster than it grew.

items.name: Flora Shard
items.lore: Dust that settled somewhere it was not disturbed.

items.name: Flora Crystal
items.lore: It is warm, and it does not stop being warm.

items.name: Forager's Ration
items.lore: Filling. That is the whole of its reputation.

items.name: Oak Circlet
items.lore: A band of green wood, bent and pinned. It tightens as it dries.

items.name: Oak Quarterstaff
items.lore: Season it a year and it stops arguing. Nobody seasons it a year.

items.name: Oak Wand
items.lore: Light enough to forget, which is the point of it.

items.name: Oak Knot
items.lore: A burl worked smooth, kept in the off hand. Carvers say the tangle remembers which way it grew, and pointing it settles the question.

items.name: Bindweed Hood
items.lore: It keeps the sun off, and the wood does the rest.

items.name: Bindweed Robe
items.lore: Woven wet and left to shrink. It fits by the third day.

items.name: Bindweed Leggings
items.lore: They whistle faintly in a wind. No one has explained it.

items.name: Bindweed Boots
items.lore: Quiet on leaf litter, which in this wood cuts both ways.

items.name: Bindweed Gloves
items.lore: The weave tightens when you grip. Let go slowly.

items.name: Sporecap Mantle
items.lore: Still shedding. Field note: the spores settle on whatever is nearest and the wearer is rarely nearest.

items.name: Heartwood Staff
items.lore: Cut from the centre, which is why it is warm. It is still growing, very slowly, in whichever direction it is pointed.

items.name: Proof of the Woods
items.lore: A knot of root that kept growing after it was cut. The guard on the north road has seen a hundred and still turns each one over twice.

items.name: Fawnhide
items.lore: Thin, and it takes a dye better than anything else this close to the water. Nobody in Hearthwood will say where they get it.

items.name: Sapwort
items.lore: Grows with its feet in the brook and its head in the sun, and tastes of neither.

items.name: Aqua Dust
items.lore: What water leaves when it is broken faster than it can close.

items.name: Aqua Shard
items.lore: Dust that stood in one place long enough to set.

items.name: Aqua Crystal
items.lore: It is cold, and it does not stop being cold.

items.name: Sapwort Draught
items.lore: Tastes like the underside of a leaf. Apprentices carry two and use neither, which is its own kind of lesson.

items.name: Fawnhide Belt
items.lore: Soft enough to sleep in. It will hold a bottle where you can reach it, which is worth more than it sounds.

items.name: Brookstone Pendant
items.lore: A river pebble with a hole worn through it, strung on gut. Looking through the hole shows the same world, calmer.

items.name: Proof of the Brook
items.lore: A pale river stone that has not warmed since it left the water. The guard on the north road weighs it in his palm and takes his time.

items.name: Copper Ore
items.lore: The hills here rust green. Forgeholm pays for it by the sack and does not say what the hurry is.

items.name: Tuskhide
items.lore: Scarred, singed, and thicker than a door. Whatever wears it walks through embers on purpose.

items.name: Pyro Dust
items.lore: What a burning thing leaves when it is put out before it finished.

items.name: Pyro Shard
items.lore: Dust that banked itself and went on quietly burning.

items.name: Pyro Crystal
items.lore: It is hot, and it does not cool.

items.name: Tuskhide Belt
items.lore: Two bottles and room for a third. The buckle outweighs the knife.

items.name: Cinder Loop
items.lore: A ring of char that never quite goes out. Wearing it feels like the moment before a pot boils over.

items.name: Proof of the Foothills
items.lore: A plate of black glass with the heat still somewhere inside it. The guard on the north road holds each one up to the light before he nods.

items.name: Bogflax Fibre
items.lore: Retted in the mire by the mire. Cloth of it never fully dries, and never quite burns either.

items.name: Fenroot
items.lore: Bitter enough to make your eyes water at arm's length. The herbalists of Galehaven buy every scrap and boil it with the windows open.

items.name: Amber
items.lore: Light that went into a tree and never came back out. Sometimes there is a wing in it.

items.name: Bogflax Hood
items.lore: Keeps the rain out. The mire finds another way in.

items.name: Bogflax Robe
items.lore: Heavy when wet, and it is always wet. You stop noticing.

items.name: Bogflax Leggings
items.lore: Mud to the knee is the local dye lot.

items.name: Bogflax Boots
items.lore: The mire keeps boots. These are the kind it gives back.

items.name: Bogflax Gloves
items.lore: Waxed against the wet. Grip first, apologise later.

items.name: Wickerbound Ring
items.lore: Willow withies in a knot that took someone a whole winter. Cut it and it grows closed by morning.

items.name: Birch Log
items.lore: First back after the burn, straight as a rule and pale as paper. The vale is a plantation nobody planted.

items.name: Brookmint
items.lore: Cold on the tongue even in this valley. It grows where the streams cut through the ash, greener than anything around it.

items.name: Charcoal
items.lore: The vale makes its own. Gathering it is not burning anything that was not already burned.

items.name: Brookmint Tonic
items.lore: Drink it and count. The cold goes down, turns around, and comes back up as warmth over the next little while.

items.name: Birch Quarterstaff
items.lore: Springy where oak is stubborn. It gives, then gives back.

items.name: Birch Wand
items.lore: Peels itself a little more each week, like it is in a hurry.

items.name: Birch Knot
items.lore: A pale whorl with a dark centre. It warms in the hand it likes.

items.name: The Charlock
items.lore: A seed case of black glass on a charred stem. Every morning it has flowered again, and every evening the flower is ash.

gatherNodes.flavor: An old stand, wind-felled and seasoning where it lies. Good logs, if your arms are willing.
A tangle thick enough to trip a horse. The trick is cutting it before it notices.
